claims.text: Grain-boundary segregation is a key mechanism governing toughness degradation in initially single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Nanoclustering is a key mechanism governing toughness degradation in initially single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Atom probe tomography can reveal the relevant grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering.
Controlled introduction of grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering will alter deformation mechanisms and microstructural evolution.
Grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering will cause brittle behavior to emerge.
Grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering will reduce toughness relative to the initial single-phase baseline.
The initial single-phase high-entropy alloy has a favorable strength–ductility combination.
The proposed behavior is relevant under both high- and low-temperature service and various loading conditions.
The effects of grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering on toughness degradation are not well understood.
